items.rationale: A1–A4/B1/B2/B8: all 16 are familiar concrete objects in ordinary school/home/garden use. Independently checked manufacturer geometry sets, floor-cleaning uses, sanitary installation families and garden tools. Each group uses one real functional predicate; all members are concept nodes. B3/B4: I walked the 16 displayed labels with hidden groups. Geometry provides an early anchor; mop/vacuum/dustpan resolve indoor-floor cleaning; bath/basin/toilet/tap form installed sanitary equipment; shovel/rake/watering can/wheelbarrow form gardening implements. Adversarial overlaps are broom versus rake (both gather debris), garden taps, and water in a watering can. They do not support an equally coherent replacement partition: rake is not an ordinary indoor-floor tool, a mobile watering can is not plumbed, and a tap is a fitting rather than a garden hand implement. B5/B6/B9: no mirrored relation sets, abstract filler or label containing a member’s complete name. B7: modest introductory gradient; cleaning/geometry are quick anchors, the tighter plumbing-versus-mobile-watering distinction needs a little more interpretation. It is an easy functional board, not a wordplay/hard board. A5/A6: no boundary trigger. Independently checked full 234-board inventory plus 122 validated tombstones including the co-candidate: no 3/4-quad reuse, maximum external board overlap 1, projected maximum use 1. Fresh exact dossier/current binding reproduce, zero lints, contested/unfair/raw-engine unfair all 0, no cross-group strong edge. Promote this exact board; the limited difficulty and contextual broom/rake boundary remain explicit agent-review judgments, not human playtest evidence.

A1–A4/B1/B2/B8: all 16 are concrete familiar household/workshop objects. Legrand material supports outlet/plug/switch components; a bulb is the circuit’s light-producing load. STANLEY/Bahco document the manual tool senses, IKEA/DEX the seating family and Tefal the cookware family. B3/B4: seating and hot-cooking vessels are immediate anchors; hammer/screwdriver/pliers/saw form manual workshop tools; the remaining four are electrical circuit components. Adversarial readings include powered saws/screwdrivers, pliers used by electricians and stool as a footrest. Those do not create an alternative partition: using a tool on wiring does not make it a circuit component, no powered appliance is shown as a tile, and the primary stool sense is seating. Oală/Cratiță/Tigaie overlap remains inside one intended group; baking tray is still a vessel for heat cooking. B5/B6/B9: no mirrored sets, bare abstract filler or full-member label leakage. B7: a low introductory gradient, from recognizable seating/cookware to the more specific component-versus-tool distinction; no obscurity provides difficulty. A5/A6: no boundary trigger. Independent full inventory + 122-tombstone census including the co-candidate finds no shared external tile, no 3/4-quad reuse and projected member use 1. The rejected writing/bed proposal is not these bytes. Fresh dossier/current binding reproduce; zero lints, contested/unfair/raw-engine unfair all 0, no strong cross-group edges. Promote this exact easy functional board. General tool labels can have powered variants, but no other on-board group competes for that interpretation; no human playtest is claimed.
